title: R1.1 Triage
summary: Topics to be covered by triage include: Triage questions/sections include:  Information from the Data Provider – in particular, do pre existing contract terms, IP, licensees, data formats exist that will impact on the terms that can be used in the contract; Information Governance requirements for the institution, related to data protection/ethics, risk, liability; Data/Technical requirements such as existing data management plans, requirements for a Trusted Research Environment; insurance  - specifically cyber insurance; key contacts/who should be involved; financial issues; TRE requirements – and more generally where the data will be stored, cyber insurance needs and requirements for future compliance.  Understanding timelines and deadlines is also a must, as is identifying any required signatories.
details: A key barrier to contracting is the lack of information gathering at the start of any contracting process, and the ‘reactive’ approach that is thus required with information emerging at different stages as the contract progresses.

title: R1.3 Technical Audits and Compliance
summary: Regular reviews should be carried out to ensure that the institution hosting the shared data remains compliant with the terms of the contract – e.g. are appropriate security measures in place, has data been deleted when scheduled.  Similarly contracts should be reviewed on a regular basis to ensure that terms reflect current legislation and any changes to how data is shared.   A checklist is required to allow researchers and others to easily determine when to raise issues with contracting and/or technical teams.
details: Contract signature is not the end of the data sharing process, but rather the beginning.  Regular review is required to ensure that the signed terms are still fit for purpose, and that the institution or federated infrastructure sharing the data is compliant with agreed measures.

title: R2.1 Policy
summary: At National Level: we recommend that a national level research data contracting policy is developed (with the guidance of the ACCoRD Community) which will include: the establishing and staffing of the advisory service; the new RTP professional; the development and use of templates specifically for research data contracting (separately from those used for research contracting); clear guidance with regards to sharing and federating personal data. At Institutional Level: we recommend that institutions mandate named points of contact and develop Key Performance Indicators to monitor the contracting process and improvements due to ACCoRD; clarity should also be provided to all parties with regards to acceptable levels of risk and regular training should be mandated for all involved staff. Finally, ethics teams should be involved when the contract relates to personal data.
details: Formalising the research data contracting process using a top-down approach with both raise the profile of the contracting challenges that are currently barriers to the UK vision for Digital Research Infrastructure and ensure that both national organisations and academic institutions pay additional attention to contracting (i.e. the impact will be similar to national mandates for more systematic research data management planning).  Clear policies reduce uncertainty and risk, and ensure fairness throughout the research data contracting ecosystem,  as well as supporting decision making and accountability

title: R2.3 Professional Development - Training and Guidance
summary: Deliver training (in person or online) and develop guidance (reference documentation) for national and institutional use. These should cover key areas that include: specialist knowledge to support specific data contracting processes and tasks; generalist knowledge to increase cross-disciplinary understanding; process descriptions to ensure that all key stakeholders are engaged as needed and timelines well understood. At National Level: we recommend that guidance and training be developed through a collaboration of the ACCoRD Community and the Advisory service, to cover: Handling Personal Data; Intellectual Property; managing Partnerships; Risk and Liability. At Institutional Level: we recommend that training and guidance be developed specifically for signatories, to ensure that they do not sign contracts without understanding the ramifications; cross-disciplinary training between the stakeholders involved in contracting is also required to prevent misunderstandings; clear documentation relating to institutional contracting processes, risk management and compliance should be developed.
details: At National Level, having shared guidance and training will not only assist contracting stakeholders, but will also be a useful resource for those data providers who may be considering sharing their data across the Federation.  At Institutional Level, the lack of understanding of the roles and perspectives of other disciplines leads in turn to not providing the required information for a research data contract, as well as unrealistic perspectives on timelines for drafting and signature as well as signatory errors.

title: R3.1 Advisory Services and RTP Role
summary: Develop a National Advisory Service, consisting of a one-stop-shop, potentially co-hosted by UKRI and the Information Commissioners Office. This service should provide advice on issues such as data protection, multi-party contracting, international contracting, and will also be a support service for academic institutions facing one-off situations that do not fall within the scope of research data contracting templates. As part of this, create create a new Research Technical Professional Role - research technical professionals (such as data stewards) form a key part of any DRI. There is a need for an intermediary and coordination role who has a multi-disciplinary perspective across the entire research data contracting process, understanding both the legal and technical aspects of research data (including sharing data across a Federated system). We recommend that the role is defined and governed within the National Advisory Service, with each institution employing multiple RTPs with this expertise.
details: The need for this service emerges from the XXX comments made during the workshop highlighting that issues relating to data protection – in particular different perspectives of different contracting parties – and the additional complexity introduced by multi-party contracts are major blockers.  Currently roles are siloed – researchers, contract teams and data managers/stewards are isolated from each other.   This leads to situations where contracting terms are not technically deliverable, and to delays and communication challenges while these issues are resolved.

title: R3.2 Automation and Evolving Digital Research Infrastructure
summary: Identify existing approaches/develop bespoke approaches to (semi-) automate the research data contracting process.  Particular challenges include tracking contract progress, and identifying key stakeholders to review the contract,  and – once terms are agreed – obtaining the required signatures. There is also a need to have an overview of all research data contracts in progress, to ensure that blockers are identified early on and overall contract time is not a blocker to research.    In parallel with automation, although not specifically identified as a contracting challenge during our research, the diversity and number of the NFCS projects highlights the effort required to develop and deliver a Digital Research Infrastructure that is robust and fit for future needs.  We recommend that a regular review of all ACCoRD recommendations is carried out, to update them as our understanding of the UK DRI evolves.
details: The advent of Large Language Models, along with general resourcing challenges, highlights the need to explore semi-automated solutions as enablers of the research data contracting process.  While the use of LLMs requires additional research – in particular in relation to trustworthiness of results – simpler solutions could involve systems that track a contract and reporting progress against KPIs, or that generate/suggest template terms and compliance checks based on the contract requirements
